title: Core path declaration
description: FR-61 requires the framework to declare which paths constitute the core and which are consumer-editable. This schema constrains that declaration so it stays a checkable input to the SC-01 diff rather than prose. FR-04 additionally requires the runtime binding layer to be enumerated, so a fourth category exists for it: the core is only meaningfully runtime-agnostic if the runtime-specific part is named.

runtimeIdentifiers.description: Identifiers, formats and capability names specific to one runtime. FR-04 forbids these inside core paths. An empty list would make the FR-04 check pass vacuously, so minItems forbids it.

selfExclusions.description: Paths exempt from the FR-04 search. Only files that must name a runtime identifier in order to forbid it belong here, and each carries its justification. Exclusions are exact paths, never patterns: a pattern would silently widen as the repository grows.

categories.description: Every tracked file must fall under exactly one category. A file matching none of them fails the check, so content cannot appear in the repository outside the declaration.

core.description: Runtime-agnostic declarative contract. Subject to FR-04, and the baseline SC-01 measures against.

binding.description: The only place a runtime identifier may appear (FR-04, CON-03). Removing it must leave the core internally consistent.

frameworkOwned.description: Executable tooling and deployment composition. Not consumer-editable, and not subject to FR-04, because implementing a binding necessarily names the runtime.

consumerEditable.description: Where a consumer's own content lives. Onboarding a workload must touch only these paths (SC-01).

repositoryMeta.description: Documentation, governance and automation. Changes here do not count against SC-01.

path.description: A repository-relative path using forward slashes. A trailing slash denotes a directory prefix.

status.description: A 'planned' entry declares intent before the content exists, which NFR-24 requires because a directory holding only a keep-file is forbidden. It must name the task that materialises it, so the declaration cannot become permanent fiction.

then.description: A present path has already been materialised; carrying a task reference would leave a stale pointer behind.
